paper: Blanchard & Katz (1992), 'Regional Evolutions', Brookings Papers on Economic Activity 1:1992
note: Provided repo was EMPTY; all code written from scratch. Panel reconstructed from public FRED/BLS APIs (paper used archival BLS 'Employment and Earnings').

step_outcomes.notes: 10-year unemployment persistence much weaker than employment persistence (R2 <=0.41 vs 0.75), matching paper's 'only transitory departures'. Pre-1976 endpoints flagged not reconstructable; nearest analogues reported. Fig 10 uses pcinc proxy.

step_outcomes.description: Trivariate VAR (emp, unemployment, participation) Fig 7 + Okun coefficient (C18).
step_outcomes.stdout: emp -1%->peak -2.1%(y3) plateau -1.8%; unemp +0.2% dies out ~y6-7; partic -0.5% recovers ~y7. per-worker shares: unemployment 0.115 participation 0.284 migration 0.601. Okun all coef=18.3 t=14.7; farm coef=14.7 t=4.4
step_outcomes.notes: Central paper result reproduced: adjustment to an employment shock is dominated by out-migration (~60%), then participation (~28%), then unemployment (~12%); unemployment/participation effects die out in 6-7 years while employment loss is permanent. Farm-state Okun coef < all-state, as paper finds. Window 1978-1990 (LAUS). Working-age pop proxied by resident population; unemployment response approximated by -le (documented).

step_outcomes.stdout: emp-income: emp -1%->trough -1.64%(y3) plateau -1.17%; income trough -0.83% ~y1-2 then reverts. suppress feedback: plateau with=-1.17% without=-1.46%
step_outcomes.notes: Emp-income (Fig 13) genuine: income troughs ~year 2 and recovers. Suppressing wage/income feedback deepens the permanent employment loss (-1.46 vs -1.17), the Fig 14 point that wage/price adjustment aids recovery. Emp-wage (Fig 11) reported with pcinc proxy (mfg AHE not reconstructable); QCEW/ASM/BEA-industry all start >=1990 or need a key, confirming no source for the 1947-1990 window.

VALIDATION: matches paper's opening facts -- MA unemployment ~3pp below US in mid-80s and ~2pp above in 1991 (paper: '3 points below... more than 2 points above'); miracle (1980-85 above US) is a blip on a chronic below-US trend (29/32 years below); late-80s bust reproduced. Manufacturing/CPS wage relative fields null & flagged (not reconstructable).
